explanation: Play at least one = 46 + 12 − 9 = 49. Neither = 87 − 49 = 38.

subject: APT
body: In a group of 85 students, 59 play football, 12 play basketball and 3 play both. How many play neither?
explanation: Play at least one = 59 + 12 − 3 = 68. Neither = 85 − 68 = 17.

subject: APT
body: In a group of 58 students, 36 play football, 11 play basketball and 6 play both. How many play neither?
explanation: Play at least one = 36 + 11 − 6 = 41. Neither = 58 − 41 = 17.

subject: APT
body: Statements: All doctors are graduates. All graduates are literate. Conclusion: All doctors are literate.
options: It follows only if some graduates are doctors
explanation: All A are B and all B are C, so all A are C.

subject: APT
body: Statements: All cats are animals. Some animals are black. Conclusion: Some cats are black.
options: It follows because all cats are animals
explanation: The black animals need not include any cats.

subject: APT
body: Statements: No fish is a bird. All sparrows are birds. Conclusion: No sparrow is a fish.
explanation: Sparrows are inside 'birds', and no bird is a fish.

subject: APT
body: Statements: Some pens are blue. All blue things are bright. Conclusion: Some pens are bright.
explanation: The blue pens must be bright.

subject: APT
body: Statements: All roses are flowers. Some flowers fade quickly. Conclusion: All roses fade quickly.
explanation: We only know some flowers fade; they may not be roses.

subject: APT
body: Statements: All teachers are readers. No reader is lazy. Conclusion: No teacher is lazy.
explanation: Teachers are readers, and no reader is lazy.

subject: APT
body: Statements: Some boys are tall. Some tall people are athletes. Conclusion: Some boys are athletes.
explanation: Two 'some' statements never give a definite conclusion.

subject: APT
body: Statements: All squares are rectangles. All rectangles are quadrilaterals. Conclusion: Some quadrilaterals are squares.
explanation: Squares are inside quadrilaterals, so some quadrilaterals are squares.

subject: APT
body: Statements: No metal is a liquid at room temperature except mercury. Iron is a metal. Conclusion: Iron is solid at room temperature.
explanation: Iron is a metal other than mercury.

subject: APT
body: Statements: All books have pages. This object has pages. Conclusion: This object is a book.
options: It is a book only on Mondays
Nothing with pages is a book
explanation: Other things (e.g. a magazine) have pages too.

subject: APT
body: A is the brother of B. B is the sister of C. C is the father of D. How is A related to D?
explanation: A is a sibling of D's father, so A is D's uncle.

subject: APT
body: P is the mother of Q. Q is the sister of R. R is the son of S. How is S related to P?
explanation: P and S are both parents of R (and Q), so S is P's husband.

subject: APT
body: X's mother is the only daughter of Y's grandmother. How is Y related to X if Y is male and X's mother is not Y's mother?
explanation: X's mother is Y's aunt, so X and Y are cousins.

subject: APT
body: Kemi's father's sister is Bola. How is Bola related to Kemi?
explanation: A father's sister is an aunt.

subject: APT
body: My mother's brother's son is my
explanation: Your uncle's son is your cousin.

subject: APT
body: A woman says of a girl, 'Her mother is the only daughter of my mother.' How is the woman related to the girl?
explanation: The only daughter of the woman's mother is the woman herself.

subject: APT
body: Pointing to a man, Amina says, 'He is the son of my father's only son.' How is the man related to Amina?
explanation: Amina is female, so her father's only son is her brother; his son is her nephew.

subject: APT
body: Tunde's father is the only son of Musa's father. How is Musa related to Tunde?
explanation: The only son of Musa's father is Musa himself, so Musa is Tunde's father.
